sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:4

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:4:1
items.html:
He did not need to also clothe in the Bina that is above Atzilut, and clothed only in the Hochma that is above Atzilut alone: Here the ARI took pains and elaborated at length to explain to us the difference between the four phases of direct light, called Hochma, Bina, Zeir Anpin and Malchut as above, and the four phases of reflected light, which are also called by those same names — Hochma, Bina, Zeir Anpin and Malchut. Now this was already explained by the ARI above (Chapter 1, item 3), and in Inner Light, item 70, that the phase of the vessels of Atzilut is made by the reflected light that rises upward to its place, in which the self of the light of Ein Sof is clothed — namely the four phases of direct light (see there, and in Inner Light). And you see how the four phases Hochma, Bina, Zeir Anpin and Malchut of direct light are clothed in the reflected light that rises by the coupling by striking, in the screen that is in the Malchut of direct light.
From this you can understand that wherever the word “clothing” is written, the meaning is that the direct light clothes in the reflected light. And when it says that Ein Sof clothed in Hochma, its meaning is that the four phases — Hochma, Bina, Zeir Anpin and Malchut of direct light that expand from Ein Sof — clothed in the Hochma of reflected light: namely, in the measure of reflected light that has the level of Hochma of direct light, in which reflected light of that level of Hochma all four phases of direct light are clothed — Hochma, Bina, Zeir Anpin and Malchut — except for the Keter of direct light, which is hidden within the Hochma of direct light, as above (Chapter 3, item 1, Inner Light, Sub Header, “And There”).
Now surely, the four phases of direct light that expand from Ein Sof also come in the way of cause and effect, cause and caused, in the order of degree, for indeed they issue and are drawn one from another — Hochma is drawn from Keter, Bina is drawn from Hochma, Zeir Anpin is drawn from Bina, and Malchut is drawn from Zeir Anpin, as above (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 50, Sub Header, “Now,” and in Inner Observation, Part 2, Sub Header “And Now” through Sub Header “And So”). However, this is not called clothing, since the four phases of direct light are not clothed one in another — for one might say, for example, that the upper light clothes in Bina in order to illuminate Zeir Anpin, since “clothed” means in a garment of reflected light that rises by the coupling by striking from the screen, which is fashioned in phase four, which is Malchut, as above in the words of the ARI (Chapter 1, item 3, and Inner Light there, item 100). But here in Bina there was no restriction at all, and needless to say there is no screen ready for the striking of the upper light into reflected light, so that one could say that the light clothed in the Bina of direct light in order to illuminate Zeir Anpin of direct light. Rather, this is called a “way of passage,” meaning that the light of Ein Sof that belongs to Zeir Anpin of direct light must necessarily pass through the sefira of Bina of direct light, since she is the cause of Zeir Anpin of direct light, and this Zeir Anpin of direct light cannot attain any light except through its cause, namely Bina — but this is not called clothing in the screen of Bina, since there is no screen there, as it is explained that there is a screen only in phase four, namely in Malchut, as above (Chapter 1, item 100).
And remember well the explained difference between the four phases of direct light and the four phases of reflected light, so that you will not be confused by the close resemblance of their names. For when we say Hochma of direct light, the meaning is the second sefira after Keter of direct light, called Hochma. But when we say Hochma of reflected light, the meaning is that there is here a coupling by striking, and ten sefirot of reflected light clothe the ten sefirot of direct light — namely twenty complete sefirot, and when they are included one in another, they are a hundred sefirot. We call all of them by the name Hochma of reflected light, because the intention is to indicate the measure of the level of the reflected light, and since it rises and clothes up to Hochma, we therefore call all hundred sefirot by the name Hochma. Remember this well, for it is the most important key in this wisdom. And in the same way you will understand Bina of reflected light, which is likewise twenty sefirot, except that Keter and Hochma are hidden within Bina. And likewise Zeir Anpin of reflected light has twenty sefirot, except that Keter, Hochma and Bina are hidden within Zeir Anpin (as above, Chapter 3, item 1, Sub Header “And There,” Inner Light).
And this is what the ARI writes: “And it did not need to clothe in the Bina that is above Atzilut, and it clothed only in the Hochma that is above Atzilut.” He means to say that for the sake of the ten sefirot of Atzilut, it clothed in the Hochma that is above Atzilut, namely in the Hochma of reflected light, as above (Inner Light, Chapter 3, item 1, Sub Header “And There”), by the coupling by striking in the screen of phase three that is in the Malchut, as written there. But it did not need to clothe in the Bina of reflected light, namely by the coupling by striking in the screen of phase two that is in the vessel of Malchut, because the level of Bina of reflected light belongs to the ten sefirot of Beria, and not to the ten sefirot of the world of Atzilut, where the level of Hochma of reflected light clothes, as above in Inner Light, Chapter 3, item 1, Sub Header “And There.”

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:4:2
items.html: And through it He shines in the Keter and Hochma of Atzilut: Meaning, that it illuminates in the ten sefirot of Atzilut at the level of Hochma, and since Keter is hidden here within Hochma, as above in the previous item, it therefore includes Keter and Hochma together in the measure of the level.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:4:3
items.html: When He wished to shine from Bina of Atzilut onward to the end of all Atzilut: Namely from the sefira of Bina of direct light to Malchut of direct light.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:4:4
items.html: Certainly He needed to clothe also in Bina of Atzilut: That it does not use the term “clothing” precisely here, as the ARI concludes immediately after this, saying: “Although it is drawn through Bina, this is not called clothing, since there is no screen there,” end quote. And this has already been explained at length above, in the previous item, that the word “clothing” indicates that the ten sefirot of direct light are clothed in the reflected light that rises by the coupling by striking in the screen. And this is what the ARI writes — since there is no screen at all here in Bina, this is not called clothing.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:4:5
items.html: Zeir Anpin and Nukva receive light only by means of Bina: For the reason that Bina is the cause of Zeir Anpin and Nukva even in the four phases of direct light, and therefore every effect must receive all that it has directly from its cause, as explained in the previous item.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:4:6
items.html: Bina served only as a passage alone: All this has been explained well in the previous item.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:4:7
items.html: Bina did not become a screen and a second garment in order to shine to Zeir Anpin: Meaning, that there is no screen there for the light of Ein Sof to expand upon for a coupling by striking, and to raise reflected light at the level of Bina, so that this reflected light of the level of Bina would be a second garment over the light of Ein Sof, in addition to the first garment, which is from the reflected light of the level of Hochma, as explained well above.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:4:8
items.html:
Through a window, without any screen at all: See in Part 2, in the table of answers, item 30, on the word “window” — that wherever the screen acts to raise reflected light from below upward, the coarseness is called by the name window, see there, also in Inner Light (Part 2, Chapter 2, item 70, Sub Header, “Hole”). And here too the coarseness acts from below upward, as above in the words of the ARI (Part 3, Chapter 1, item 3), and therefore the ARI calls there the coarseness of the phase of Zeir Anpin and the phase of Malchut by the name window and narrow hole (Chapter 1, item 4), since the screens that are below the level of Hochma serve there only from below upward, as written before us.
And one should not raise a difficulty here from what is explained elsewhere, that even in the ten sefirot of Atzilut there are five partzufim, each of which has a phase of coupling by striking. For there is a great and considerable difference between them, since all these five partzufim of Atzilut are five parts of the ten sefirot of the level of Hochma, and this will be explained in its place, and we shall not elaborate here.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:4:9
items.html:
In Beria, Ein Sof clothes in another garment in Bina of Atzilut: Meaning, that the screen and the Malchut are refined to phase two, which is called Bina, and the light of Ein Sof expands for a coupling by striking on that screen, and raises reflected light at the level of Bina, as above (Inner Light, Chapter 3, item 6) — that this reflected light is another, new garment over the light of Ein Sof, very different from the garment of reflected light of Atzilut itself. For the garment of Atzilut is from the striking in the screen of phase three, which draws the light of Hochma into all the ten sefirot, while this new garment is from the striking in the screen of phase two, whose level does not reach to clothe the Hochma of direct light, but only Bina of direct light alone, and therefore there is no light of Hochma in it whatsoever.
Now this coupling must necessarily take place in Atzilut, as above in Inner Light (Chapter 3, item 6), but all these ten sefirot that are clothed in the garment of the level of Bina are drawn from the screen downward and come into the world of Beria, as explained in the above Inner Light.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:4:10
items.html: Bina becomes a sealed screen and a complete garment: Meaning, although the reflected light rises at first from the screen that is in Bina and upward, namely in the world of Atzilut as above, so that even the sefirot of Atzilut must necessarily be clothed in this garment of the level of Bina, nevertheless the coarseness and closure of this screen does not rise there even in the slightest, since coarseness and defect can never act at all upon what is above them. And such a phase of reception is called window and hole (as written in Inner Light, Part 2, Chapter 2, item 70), meaning without any coarseness whatsoever. This is not so with the reflected light that descends below the screen between Atzilut and Beria, namely the ten sefirot that come into the world of Beria: there, the power and coarseness of the screen is the entire root of the expansion of the light of Ein Sof in them. Therefore the screen becomes a closure and a complete garment, which restricts the light of Ein Sof from illuminating there even the slightest of the light of Hochma — for it is a screen of phase two, whose reflected light does not reach Hochma, but only Bina of direct light alone, as above. And this is what the ARI writes, “that a closed screen was made,” meaning that it closes off the light of Atzilut, namely the light of Hochma, from appearing in the world of Beria even in the slightest, for the reason that this screen influences Beria from above downward, as explained.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:4:11
items.html: It is considered as receiving only from Hochma alone: Meaning, from the level of Hochma alone, but from Keter, Atzilut cannot receive, because the screen of phase three serves there from above downward, since it clothed in phase three that is above Atzilut as above, and therefore a closed screen was made over the light of Keter, and it is considered that it receives only from Hochma alone.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:4:12
items.html: Ein Sof and Hochma clothe within it: Meaning, that Keter and Hochma are hidden in the level of Bina, since this reflected light does not reach them but only the level of Bina alone, as above, and therefore Beria receives only from Bina alone, and cannot receive from Keter and Hochma, because the screen closes them off as above, for the reason that it is above Beria. And this is what the ARI writes, that a screen was made separating Keter and Hochma from Beria. And remember, that Keter is called Ein Sof, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:4:13
items.html: The supernal Ima nests in the throne: For an illumination that is not constant is called by the name nesting, similar to a bird that does not sit constantly upon its chicks but only occasionally. And since the coupling of the aforementioned phase two is not a constant illumination in the world of Beria, it is therefore called by the term nesting, and it says that the Upper Mother “nests” on the throne. Bina is called the Upper Mother, and for the reason that Bina is called so, see in the book Panim Masbirot, page 61, Sub Header “And the Reason for the Naming,” and we shall not elaborate here.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:4:14
items.html:
Zeir Anpin does not interpose for it: As was explained above concerning Bina of Atzilut, that the coupling made in the screen of phase two for the sake of Beria — the reflected light rises and clothes up to Bina — nevertheless this does not become a partition upon the light of Hochma toward Zeir Anpin of Atzilut, which is found after that Bina. And it was explained that this is for the reason that the screen that serves from below upward does not carry, together with the reflected light that rises through it, any new limit or coarseness whatsoever to those who receive from it. And although Zeir Anpin of Atzilut also receives from the power of this reflected light, nevertheless it is not diminished by its cause so that it could not draw the light of Hochma, because a phase of reception by the power of a screen from below the degree is called only window and hole, but it does not restrict or close off anything by its cause. And so you should understand regarding all screens in all places, that the limits that are always made because of screens — those limits are not felt at all except by those who receive from below the screen, but not at all by those who receive from above the existence of the screen.
And this is what the ARI writes, that although “the light returned to clothe in Zeir Anpin of Beria,” and makes a coupling by striking in the screen of phase one, so that this reflected light has the level of Zeir Anpin — behold, although Malchut of Beria also receives from this reflected light, nevertheless, since this screen serves from the phase of below upward, it does not restrict Malchut of Beria at all, so that it could not draw to itself the light of Bina, because “Zeir Anpin does not partition” Malchut of Beria with his screen that is found from below upward, for it is only “a way of passage alone,” meaning from the phase of a window and not from the phase of a screen, as above (Part 3, item 4, in Inner Light, item 6). And so it is in all places.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:4:15
items.html: The particulars of Yetzira from within itself: The matter of the reflected light that descends from above downward, whose way it is to expand the screen and the vessel of Malchut, until they expand of themselves into ten sefirot from above downward, from Keter to Malchut, as above in Inner Light (Chapter 3, item 5) — this expansion of Malchut is called in every place “expansion from itself within itself,” meaning that the single vessel that is called Malchut expands of itself, from itself within itself, into ten sefirot. And you already know that the limited ten sefirot in every world are made only by the reflected light that expands to them from above downward, as above; therefore these ten sefirot are called by the name the individual ten sefirot from itself within itself, whether in Atzilut, in Yetzira, or in Assiya.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:4:16
items.html: A complete garment also in Zeir Anpin of Beria: The reflected light that expands from the screen downward is called a complete garment, since it restricts, with its own particular coarseness, the lights that it clothes, so that they cannot draw any light different from its limit. This is not so with the reflected light that rises from below upward: although it too is a garment over the ten sefirot of direct light, nevertheless this garment does not restrict at all the light that it clothes, as above, and it is therefore considered a garment that is not complete, but only the phase of a root of a garment. And the matter of the expansion of the ten sefirot of Yetzira and Assiya has already been explained well above, see there.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:4:17
items.html: Six Sefirot nest in Yetzira: Zeir Anpin is called by the name six sefirot, and is called so because of the absence of the three first [sefirot], Keter-Hochma-Bina, and because of the absence of Malchut, and it has only the six sefirot Hesed-Gevura-Tifferet-Netzah-Hod-Yesod alone. And the word nesting has already been explained above.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:4:18
items.html: And the lower Ima nests in the Ofan: Malchut of Atzilut is sometimes called the Lower Mother, because Malchut of Atzilut is the main root for all that exist in Beria, Yetzira and Assiya. And in the name of Malchut of Atzilut, Malchut of Yetzira is also called by the name Lower Mother, since they are one root, and we shall not elaborate here.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:4:19
items.html: Atzilut, Beria, Yetzira, Asiya, are alluded to in the four letters of the Havaya: As he goes on to explain, that the name HaVaYaH includes ten sefirot, and the four worlds Atzilut, Beria, Yetzira and Assiya are the phase of the ten sefirot that include all existence. And although in each and every world by itself there are individual Atzilut, Beria, Yetzira and Assiya, and particulars of particulars, nevertheless one must know that all of them together are arranged in only ten sefirot, which the four letters of HaVaYaH allude to, as explained. And this knowledge is very necessary, that it should always be before the eyes of the student, since one must always compare the individual ten sefirot to the inclusive ten sefirot, for they always have corresponding values to one another and are learned from one another.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:4:20
items.html: The light of Atzilut is by means of the supernal Hochma as above: Meaning, although in Atzilut alone there are ten sefirot, alluded to by the four letters of HaVaYaH, nevertheless, since the level of all these ten sefirot is up to Hochma, as explained above, therefore it is all considered as the light of Hochma, which the Yod of the name HaVaYaH alludes to. For the lights that are smaller than Hochma do not rise so much in name in relation to the important light of Hochma, which is far greater than they are. And for this reason Beria is called by the name the light of Bina alone, and likewise all of them — namely, by the name of the most important lights among them, as explained.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:4:21
items.html: Were it not for all these screens and garments, they would not be able to receive the upper light: Meaning, that no world can receive any light except from what the screen that is found above it grants to it, as explained above.
